newsitem.title: USA: Alleged Versace killer was wounded before death.
newsitem.headline: Alleged Versace killer was wounded before death.

text.p: Andrew Cunanan, suspected killer of Gianni Versace and four other men, was already wounded when he killed himself on a Miami Beach houseboat on July 23, the FBI said on Wednesday.
"He did have a wound and there was evidence that he was treating it himself," FBI spokeswoman Anne Figueiras said. "We found gauze and bandages. I believe it was in his abdomen."

Blood-soaked gauze pads, cotton swabs and bandages, as well as a bottle holding 19 penicillin capsules, were among the items police found in the houseboat when they searched it after Cunanan's death, according to a list released by the U.S. Attorney's office in Miami.

The list also included soda and ice tea bottles, a cracker box and the .40-calibre weapon police said Cunanan used to kill himself. It was released as law enforcement officials tried to establish Cunanan's movements during an alleged cross-country killing spree that began in April and ended July 15, the day the Italian fashion designer was shot.

Figueras would not confirm local media speculation that Cunanan was wounded during one of the murders. She also declined comment on whether any of the items at the scene were linked to any other crimes.
Cunanan had been on the FBI's 10 Most Wanted list of fugitives even before the Versace slaying.

He was wanted for the murders in Minnesota of his friends Jeffrey Trail and David Madson, as well as for the slaying in Chicago of real estate developer Lee Miglin and the murder of William Reese, a cemetery caretaker found dead in New Jersey on May 9.

Chicago police confirmed on Tuesday they had matched at least one fingerprint found in Miglin's home with prints taken off the body of Andrew Cunanan. Police had been stymied in collecting evidence directly connecting Miglin's May 3 murder to Cunanan.
Miglin was stabbed, his neck slashed, his chest crushed and his body found wrapped with tape in his garage. Chicago police said they would likely conclude their investigation within a week.
The Chicago Tribune quoted a police department source as saying the department did not believe Cunanan was wounded during his slaying of Miglin.
